Team: Galaxy Byeolbit
Project: FlameGuard (NASA Space Apps). We are building an SI-powered dashboard to analyze NASA's microgravity combustion data for Moon/Mars fire safety.

Skills needed in new members:

1. Data Scientists/Aerospace enthusiasts: To help refine ranking algorithms and interpret complex NASA PSI datasets.

2. UI/UX Designers: For futuristic graphics and visual polish.

3. Pitch/Video Experts: For storytelling and a killer 7-minute demo video.
summary:
In space, fire does not rise. Without gravity-driven buoyancy, flames form spherical shells that spread unpredictably with ventilation airflow, produce dense soot, and can persist after extinction as invisible cool flames that risk reigniting. Designing safe lunar bases, Mars habitats, and spacesuits requires quick access to decades of complex NASA combustion research currently buried across hundreds of technical papers.

To solve this, we built FlameGuard—an interactive, Super Intelligence (SI)-powered fire safety console for aerospace engineers and mission planners. Powered by NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database, FlameGuard lets users query, summarize, and interpret microgravity combustion behavior in plain English, filtering results across realistic mission environments including the ISS, lunar habitats, and EVA spacesuits.

FlameGuard features four isolated dossiers covering Apollo 1, Apollo 13, Mir, and ISS combustion science, paired with 24 archival NASA figures. To prevent hallucinations, our Evidence Ledger links every response directly to raw NASA test reports, while an interactive simulator maps flammability risks as oxygen and pressure shift. FlameGuard turns scattered flight data into clear, reliable safety decisions.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

In space, fire does not rise. Without gravity-driven buoyancy, hot air cannot lift away and fresh oxygen is not drawn naturally into the base of a flame. Instead, flames form quiet, spherical diffusion shells that generate up to eight times more soot than Earth fires and produce invisible "cool flames" capable of sudden reignition.

FlameGuard is an interactive microgravity fire safety console built for aerospace engineers, habitat architects, and researchers. It takes decades of complex, scattered NASA combustion research and turns it into fast, verifiable decision support.

How it works under the hood:

  • Data Ingestion: We extracted text and high-resolution technical figures from official NASA Technical Memorandums and the Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database using PyMuPDF.
  • Vector Search: Extracted passages are converted into 384-dimensional vector embeddings using HuggingFace’s all-MiniLM-L6-v2 locally on Python 3.11, then indexed in a serverless Pinecone database under nasa-combustion-rag.
  • Mission Control Query Console: Users can ask natural-language questions and filter results across specific flight environments—such as the ISS (21% O₂ at 14.7 psi), an Artemis Moon Base (34% O₂ at 10.2 psi), or an EVA Spacesuit (100% O₂ at 4.3 psi)—as well as safety pillars (Prevention, Detection, Suppression).
  • Deterministic Synthesis: We route queries to Llama 3 running on Groq LPU set strictly to temperature 0.0. If the retrieved NASA context does not contain the answer, the model is hard-coded to state that the data is not available, rather than fabricating numbers.

2. How is our project creative?

Rather than building another generic chatbot, we introduced three targeted engineering features:

  • Section-Scoped RAG Isolation: Historical spacecraft fires have distinct physics and failure modes. We built four isolated dossiers—ISS Combustion Science, Apollo 1, Apollo 13, and Mir Space Station. When an engineer queries the Apollo 13 dossier, the search engine locks exclusively to Apollo 13 records. This prevents the system from confusing facts across different spaceflight eras or mixing Apollo tank failures with Mir candle fires.
  • Interactive Flammability Risk Simulator: Instead of just text output, we built an interactive simulation tool with dynamic sliders for Oxygen Concentration (21% to 100%) and Cabin Pressure (4.3 to 14.7 psi) that calculates the Relative Flammability Index (RFI) in real time.
  • Evidence Ledger: Alongside every generated answer, our Evidence Ledger displays the exact retrieved NASA text chunks, source citations, and pipeline telemetry (Pinecone vs Fallback), giving users complete transparency.

3. What factors did our team consider?

  • Zero Tolerance for Hallucinations: In life-support engineering, a fabricated flammability threshold or ignition temperature can cost lives. We eliminated guesswork by combining deterministic temperature 0.0 synthesis with an offline fallback layer of 17 pre-verified PSI benchmark records.
  • Atmospheric Reality: Materials that are safe in Earth’s atmosphere (like standard wire insulation or Nomex) can become explosive fuel in oxygen-rich space habitats. We designed our filters around real NASA mission operating pressures and gas concentrations.
  • Respect for Flight History: We curated 24 authentic NASA archival photographs and engineering diagrams with verified credits and full-screen lightboxes, honoring the crews of Apollo 1, Apollo 13, and Mir.

4. What benefits does it have?

  • Saves Engineering Hours: Replaces days of manual searching across fragmented PDF archives with instant, citation-backed answers.
  • Prevents Design Flaws: Helps spacecraft designers evaluate material flammability under microgravity airflow before costly physical testing.
  • Auditability: Every claim links directly to its source paper, allowing safety boards to verify findings immediately.

5. What is the intended impact?

  • Space Exploration: Directly supports fire risk mitigation for NASA’s Artemis lunar missions, deep-space transit habitats, and commercial orbital stations.
  • Earth Spinoffs: Microgravity combustion physics directly benefits Earth safety. Understanding spherical flame extinction and low-velocity smoke transport helps design better particulate respirators for wildland firefighters and non-toxic water-mist fire suppression systems that replace hazardous chemicals.

6. Tools, Coding Languages, and Software Used

  • Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS 4, Lucide React, HTML5 Canvas.
  • Backend API: Python 3.11, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, SlowAPI rate limiting (5 req/min/IP).
  • AI & RAG Pipeline: Sentence-Transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2), Pinecone Serverless, Groq Cloud LPU (Llama 3), LangChain.
  • Document Processing: PyMuPDF (fitz), NASA PSI Open Data.
  • Quality & Testing: 98 pytest backend tests, 62 Vitest frontend tests, oxlint (0 errors).
  • GitHub Repository: https://github.com/harshita713lab/NASA-Hackathon-flameguard
  • Live Deployed App: https://nasa-hackathon-flameguard.vercel.app/
